title: Locality and zero-stalk vanishing of the local term
statement:
Let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times X$ be an admissible correspondence with
$\operatorname{Fix}(c)=F$, coefficient $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and
$u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$ ([def-trf-correspondence]), and let $y\in F(k)$ be a
geometric fixed point which is an open-and-closed component of $F$. Say
that $c$ is *contracting at $y$* if $c_1^{-1}(y)$ is the reduced point $y$,
$c_2(y)=y$, and the ideal sheaves on $C$ satisfy

$$
c_2^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)^n\subset\mathcal I_{y,C}^{\,n+1}\qquad\text{for some }n\geq1,
$$

where $\mathcal I_{y,C}=c_1^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)\mathcal O_C$ is the ideal of
the reduced point $y\subset C$. The stabilizing
inclusion $c_2^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)\subset\mathcal I_{y,C}$ follows from
$c_2(y)=y$, and the condition holds with $n=1$ whenever the map induced by
$c_2$ on the cotangent space at $y$ is zero.

1. (Contracting local terms.) If $c$ is contracting at $y$, then the
restriction $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_y$, and hence the local term
$\operatorname{LT}_y(u)$ of [def-trf-local-term], depend only on the stalk
$K_{\bar y}$ and on the stalk map $u_{\bar y}:K_{\bar y}\to K_{\bar y}$
induced by restriction of the correspondence to $Z=\{y\}$: explicitly, take the exceptional adjoint $\widehat u:Rc_{1!}c_2^*K\to K$, pull it back along $Z\hookrightarrow X$, and use compact-support base change and $c_1^{-1}(Z)=y$ to obtain $u_{\bar y}:K_{\bar y}\to K_{\bar y}$. Thus this is the induced point-correspondence map, not an identification of the ordinary stalk of $c_1^!K$ with $K_{\bar y}$:
$\operatorname{LT}_y(u)=\operatorname{tr}_A(u_{\bar y}\mid K_{\bar y})$.
No invertibility of $u$ is required.
1. (Zero-stalk vanishing.) If $c$ is contracting at $y$ and $K_{\bar y}=0$,
then $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_y=0$ and $\operatorname{LT}_y(u)=0$, for
every coefficient morphism $u$.
1. (Smooth-curve form.) In the smooth-curve setting of
[d-curve-pieces] — $X_0$ smooth of pure dimension one, $m\ge1$,
$x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with geometric point $\bar x$ — let
$v:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ be either the scheme-Frobenius map
$u_m=\varphi^{[m]}\circ\kappa^{(m)}_K$ of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map]
(the map written $\varphi_m$ in [d-curve-pieces]) or an arbitrary,
not necessarily invertible, Frobenius coefficient morphism
$L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ (in the sense of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] for $\Phi^m$, the
$q^m$-power Frobenius of $X_0\times_{k_0}\mathbf F_{q^m}$; for
instance the iterate $\psi_m$ of a Frobenius coefficient morphism
$\psi$), and consider the graph correspondence of
$(\Phi^m,v)$ of [def-trf-graph-correspondence], assumed admissible
as throughout so that its trace class is defined. If $K_{\bar x}=0$,
then the local term $\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(v)$ at the fixed
point $\bar x$ is zero.

proof.text: Localize the support around the point component. Put $Z=\{y\}\subset X$. Since $X$ is separated, $\Delta_X$ is a closed immersion, so $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ is closed in $C$ ([def-trf-fixed-scheme]); $F\setminus\{y\}$ is closed in $F$ because $\{y\}$ is open in $F$. Hence $W=C\setminus(F\setminus\{y\})$ is an open subscheme of $C$ containing $y$, and $F\cap W=\{y\}$ is open and closed in $F$. By the open-restriction lemma [lem-trf-trace-class-open-restriction], $\operatorname{Fix}(c|_W)=\{y\}$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{c|_W}(u|_W)=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_y$, the restricted section of [def-trf-local-term]; so the restricted trace class and the local term at $y$ are unchanged when $(c,u)$ is replaced by $(c|_W,u|_W)$. The point map is unchanged as well: the exceptional adjoint of $u|_W$ is $\widehat u$ precomposed with $Rc_{1!}$ of the counit $j_{W!}j_W^*c_2^*K\to c_2^*K$, which is an isomorphism over $c_1^{-1}(Z)=y\subset W$, so pulling back to $Z$ and applying compact-support base change gives the same $u_{\bar y}$. The contraction hypotheses restrict to $W$: $(c_1|_W)^{-1}(y)=c_1^{-1}(y)\cap W=y$, $c_2(y)=y$, and the ideal inclusion is an inclusion of ideal sheaves, which restricts to the open $W$. Thus it suffices to work with $F=y$, and this holds scheme-theoretically: $y$ is an open-and-closed point component and $\operatorname{LT}_y(u)$ of [def-trf-local-term] is defined on the reduced point component $B_y\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$, so $F\cap W=B_y$ is the reduced point, as Step 2 requires. Since $c_2(y)=y$, the image of $c_2^{\cdot}I_Z$ in $\mathcal O_y$ is zero, and $J=c_1^{\cdot}I_Z\mathcal O_C$ is the ideal of the reduced point $y$, giving the stabilizing inclusion $c_2^{\cdot}I_Z\subseteq J$.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.3, first paragraph of proof; §1.2.2(b) and open restriction §1.1.9

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-dnc-fixed-locus-reduction] with $y_C=y$ and $y_X=c_1(y)=c_2(y)$, using the stabilization and contraction inclusions from Step 1. It identifies $c^{-1}(Z\times Z)=y$, the special source $N_{y/C}$, the support of $b_2$ on $Z$, and $b_1^{-1}Z=y$. For the Rees lift of [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry], it gives the closed immersion $y_D\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c)$, generically an isomorphism and an isomorphism on reductions.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.3(b), proof after Corollary 1.4.5; Lemma 1.4.3 and Corollary 1.4.5

proof.text: The fixed-locus specialization is therefore invertible: the constant-family specialization assertion applies to the closed immersion of the constant point deformation into the lifted fixed locus, since it is generically an isomorphism and an isomorphism on reductions. Thus $\operatorname{sp}_{\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c)}$ is an isomorphism on Borel--Moore sections.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.3(b), specialization paragraph; Proposition 1.4.2 and Example 1.3.3

proof.text: All special-fibre normal-cone schemes and their leg, product, diagonal and structure morphisms are separated of finite type over $k$. The special-fibre trace-domain lemma supplies compactifications and finite dimension bounds, etale-origin witnesses, and the constructible relative exceptional adjunction and preservation needed for the finite-stage composition, compact-support and exchange package. Hence the specialized coefficient and its trace class are defined in the same bounded constructible finite-Tor category.

First prove zero-stalk vanishing directly. Suppose $K|_Z=0$. Write $M=\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}K$. The zero-section theorem gives $z^*M=K|_Z=0$. On the reduction of the source normal cone, $b_2$ factors through the reduced point $Z$ because its image is supported there: on an affine chart every pulled-back element of the ideal of $Z$ lies in every prime and hence in the nilradical, which vanishes on the reduction. Thus the pullback of $b_2^*M$ to that reduction is zero, and the reduction equivalence implies $b_2^*M=0$. Consequently $\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde c}u$ is the zero map from a zero object. The trace construction is a composition of additive maps on sections, so its trace class is zero. Trace-specialization compatibility and the invertibility from Step 3 imply $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_y=0$. On the point component, the point-local-term identification sends this zero section to $0\in A$. This proves clause (2) without any invertibility of $u$.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.3(b), normal-cone vanishing paragraph; Propositions 1.3.5 and 1.4.2

proof.text: For arbitrary $K$, use $i:Z=y\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$. Stabilization implies the invariant inclusion required by the filtered-lift lemma. Apply that lemma to lift the exceptional adjoint of $u$ to the canonical two-step localization filtration, whose graded objects are $K_Z=Ri_*i^*K$ and $K_U=j_!j^*K$. Its graded coefficient morphisms are precisely $u^Z=[i]_!(u|_Z)$ and $u^U=[j]_!(u|_U)$. Applying filtered trace additivity gives $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)+\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^U)$. This uses a filtered lift, not merely a morphism of triangles. Apply [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] to the Cartesian square formed by $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. Its upper-left corner is empty, so its extension-by-zero side is the zero complex and it gives $i^*j_!j^*K=0$. Thus $K_U|_Z=0$; Step 5 applied to $K_U$ gives $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^U)|_y=0$. Hence $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_y=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)|_y$.

The restricted correspondence on $Z$ has source $c_1^{-1}Z=y$, both legs the identity of the point, coefficient $P=i^*K=K_{\bar y}$, and map $u_{\bar y}$ defined by restriction of the exceptional adjoint and compact-support base change. The point inclusions into $X$ and $C$ are closed immersions, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Its map to $c$ is the proper diagram $(i,y\hookrightarrow C)$. The coefficient pushforward recipe gives $u^Z$ on $Ri_*P$, exactly the graded morphism of Step 6. Proper trace compatibility says $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)=h_*\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{id}_y}(u_{\bar y})$. Since both fixed schemes are $y$, $h$ is the identity, and this pushforward is the identity. Thus the original restricted trace is the trace class of the identity point correspondence.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.3(b), closed-piece paragraph, using Proposition 1.2.5 and §1.5.6

proof.text: By [fix-lem-finite-tor-perfect], $P=K_{\bar y}$ is perfect: the hypothesis $K\in D^b_{ctf}$ is precisely its finite coefficient hypothesis. For the identity point correspondence, the diagonal-pairing identity gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{id}_y}(u_{\bar y})=\langle u_{\bar y},1_P\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$. The pairing normalization at the point identifies this with $\operatorname{tr}_A(u_{\bar y}\mid P)$. Finally the point-local-term identification says integration on $y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is this same scalar. Combined with Step 7 this proves clause (1), including dependence of the restricted trace class on $(P,u_{\bar y})$. The trace of a map on the zero complex is zero, either from its defining composite through $0$ or Step 5. Neither filtered lifting, specialization, nor point normalization required an inverse of the coefficient map.

In clause (3), the graph definition gives $C=X$, $c_1=1_X$ and $c_2=\Phi^m$. The fixed-point theorem identifies $F$ with the finite disjoint union of reduced copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ indexed by $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$. Hence $\bar x$ is a reduced open-and-closed point component and its local term is defined; no properness of $X$ is needed.

Set $Q=q^m\geq2$. Choose an affine neighbourhood of $x$ in $X_0\times_{k_0}\mathbf F_Q$, generated by functions $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ over $\mathbf F_Q$, and put $a_i=t_i(x)\in\mathbf F_Q$. After base change to $k$, the ideal of $\bar x$ is generated by $t_i-a_i$. The scheme Frobenius is the base change of $Q$-power Frobenius on this model, so $(\Phi^m)^*(t_i-a_i)=t_i^Q-a_i=(t_i-a_i)^Q$. Thus $(\Phi^m)^{\cdot}I_{\bar x}\mathcal O_X\subseteq I_{\bar x}^{Q}\subseteq I_{\bar x}^2$. With $c_1=1_X$, its inverse image of $\bar x$ is the reduced point itself, and $c_2(\bar x)=\bar x$. This is contraction with $n=1$. Apply clause (2), proved in Step 5, to the given coefficient map $v$ and the zero stalk. It gives $\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(v)=0$ for both choices of $v$, proving clause (3).

proof_origin.place: Proof of Theorem 2.1.3(b), §§1.3--1.4 and §5.3.3; Frobenius application follows the current blueprint coordinate calculation.

proof.text:
*The stalk of the trace-class source.* By [def-trf-trace-class-source]
the source is $\mathcal H_c(K)=R\mathcal Hom_A(c_2^*K,c_1^!K)$. Its stalk
at $y$ is **not** $R\mathcal Hom_A(K_{\bar y},K_{\bar y})$: restriction to
a point commutes with $i^!$ on internal Hom, but not with $i^*$. For
$X=\mathbf A^1$, $j:\mathbf G_m\hookrightarrow X$, $K=j_!A$ and the graph
of a Frobenius (so that $c_2^*K\simeq K$ and $c_1^!K=K$), internal-Hom
adjunction gives $R\mathcal Hom_A(j_!A,j_!A)\simeq Rj_*A$, whose
degree-zero stalk at $0$ is $A$ (the punctured strictly henselian curve is
connected), although $K_0=0$. Hence (1) and (2) cannot be read off from
the stalk: the trace map of [lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality] is
local on $F$, but its source at $y$ sees more than $(K_{\bar y},u_{\bar y})$.
A nonzero source can still map to zero, and for contracting correspondences
it does; this is the content of (1) and (2).

*(1) and (2).* These are the contracting-correspondence theorem of
Varshavsky, [Thm. 2.1.3](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0505564), translated
into the present conventions. In Varshavsky's convention a $c$-morphism is
$c_1^*\mathcal F\to c_2^!\mathcal F$; interchanging the legs, his
hypothesis "$c$ stabilizes $Z$ and is contracting near $Z$" for
$Z=\{y\}$ reads
$c_2^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)\subset c_1^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)\mathcal O_C$ and
$c_2^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)^n\subset(c_1^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)\mathcal O_C)^{n+1}$,
which is the hypothesis above. His conclusion, for the open-and-closed
component $\beta=\{y\}$ of $F$, which meets $Z$, is
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_y=\operatorname{Tr}_{c|_Z}(u|_Z)|_y$ and
$\operatorname{LT}_y(u)=\operatorname{LT}_y(u|_Z)$, where
$c|_Z:c_1^{-1}(Z)_{\mathrm{red}}\to Z\times Z$ is the correspondence
induced on $Z$ and $u|_Z$ the restricted coefficient morphism (his 1.5.6).
Since $c_1^{-1}(y)=y$ is reduced, $c|_Z$ is the identity correspondence of
the point $y\cong\Spec k$, with coefficient $K_{\bar y}$ and morphism the
stalk map $u_{\bar y}$; its local term is
$\operatorname{tr}_A(u_{\bar y}\mid K_{\bar y})$ by
[lem-trf-local-term-point]. This proves (1), and (2) is the case
$K_{\bar y}=0$, where $\operatorname{tr}_A(0\mid0)=0$. Varshavsky's theorem
is proved by specialization to the normal cone of $Z$ (his §§1.3–1.4 and
2.1); it holds for every $c$-morphism and for the finite coefficient rings
$A=A_{E,n}$ (his §1.1), and nothing is inverted. Its proof reduces, via
the additivity of trace classes along the open–closed decomposition
$X=Z\sqcup U$ and proper pushforward from $Z$, precisely to the vanishing
(2) for $j_!j^*K$, which is then shown by the normal-cone argument; the
blueprint quotes this argument and does not reprove it.

*(3).* The graph correspondence of $(\Phi^m,v)$ has
$C=X$, $c_1=\operatorname{id}_X$, $c_2=\Phi^m$ and fixed scheme
$\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)$ by [def-trf-graph-correspondence]. By
[thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] this fixed scheme is the disjoint
union of copies of $\Spec k$, one for each point of
$X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$; in particular it is finite over $k$, hence
proper with finitely many open-and-closed components, so the local
terms of [def-trf-local-term] are defined, and the geometric point
$\bar x$ over $x$ is one of these components, an isolated reduced fixed
point. The graph is contracting at $\bar x$: $c_1^{-1}(\bar x)=\bar x$,
$\Phi^m(\bar x)=\bar x$, and if $t_i$ are affine coordinates with
$a_i=t_i(x)\in\mathbf F_{q^m}$, then
$\Phi^{m\cdot}(t_i-a_i)=t_i^{q^m}-a_i=(t_i-a_i)^{q^m}$, so
$\Phi^{m\cdot}(\mathcal I_{\bar x})\mathcal O_X\subset\mathcal I_{\bar x}^{\,q^m}\subset\mathcal I_{\bar x}^{\,2}$
as $q^m\geq2$; this holds for every separated finite-type $X_0$, not only
for curves. Its stalk map is
$v_{\bar x}:K_{\bar x}=(L\Phi^{m*}K)_{\bar x}\to K_{\bar x}$, using
$\Phi^m(\bar x)=\bar x$. Applying (2) with $y=\bar x$ and $u=v$ gives
$\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(v)=0$ when $K_{\bar x}=0$; since (1) and
(2) use no invertibility of $u$, this holds both for the
scheme-Frobenius map $u_m$ and for an arbitrary Frobenius coefficient
morphism.
